subject: Week 14: SFCM Smart Start registration closes this month
bodyText:
This week
Sleep cycles are shortening from the newborn 50–60 minutes toward the adult-like ~45 minutes, and many infants start waking between cycles this week — 4–8 wakings a night is within the expected band for weeks 14–18, biological rather than behavioral. Daytime, look for pushing up on forearms, fascinated hand-watching, and ah-goo vocal play; front-to-back rolling remains emerging for some (CDC checkpoint: 6 months).

Watch-fors this week
- [low concern] Multiple night wakings, shortened naps, and distractible feeds — the regression's hallmark trio.
- [monitor] A daytime feeding strike that persists past 48 hours.
- [monitor] Any rolling attempt while swaddled — retire the swaddle for a sleep sack the same day.
- [call within 24h] Persistent vomiting, or fever with poor feeding.
- [call now] Fever ≥102°F rectal at 90+ days, lethargy disproportionate to a bad night, or labored breathing; blue lips or unresponsiveness — 911.

Enrichment opportunities
- Register for SFCM Smart Start's 0–12-month Saturday cohort before August ends — the only SF infant music program with a fixed registration window (semester starts early September; ~$845 all-in). A missed August means a semester's delay. Active participatory music is the best-evidenced paid class at this age; passive listening is not the ingredient. SFCM Smart Start: https://sfcm.edu/study/pre-college/early-childhood
- Audit the sleep environment before the regression peaks: crib-only sleep, room at 68–72°F, white noise at or under 50 dB measured at the crib, room-darkening shades. AAP: Getting Your Baby to Sleep: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/sleep/Pages/Getting-Your-Baby-to-Sleep.aspx
- Hand him a teether or soft fabric book and watch for hand-to-hand transfer attempts — most infants transfer objects between hands by 6 months, and the precursor practice is now.
- Pause on each page at reading time — point, name the object, wait for a response. This is the first scaffold of dialogic reading. AAP early literacy: https://www.aap.org/en/patient-care/early-childhood/early-literacy/

Upcoming
- Day 100 (Aug 19, 2026): the 100-day mark (baekil) falls Wednesday — photo session this week if planned; bring two to three outfit changes and budget 60–90 minutes with soothing breaks.
- Day 112–126 (Aug 31–Sep 14, 2026): 4-month well visit; vaccines: RV #2, DTaP #2, Hib #2, PCV #2, IPV #2 — book now if you haven't.
- Early September 2026: SFCM Smart Start fall semester begins — registration must land in August.

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- Uses arm to swing at hanging toys
  AAP window: day 90-150
  What to look for: Pre-reaching swiping — not yet visually-guided grasp.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/swings-at-toys/complete

- Laughs out loud
  AAP window: day 90-180
  What to look for: Full belly laugh, not just a smile with sound. Often triggered by gentle physical play or peekaboo.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/6-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/laughs/complete

- Reaches to grab a toy he wants
  AAP window: day 90-180
  What to look for: Visually-guided reaching, eye-hand coordination.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/6-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/reaches-for-toy/complete

- Rolls from tummy to back
  AAP window: day 90-180
  What to look for: Usually appears first — back-to-tummy follows later. Once rolling begins, stop swaddling for sleep.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/6-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/rolls-tummy-to-back/complete

- Looks at you, moves, or makes sounds to keep your attention
  AAP window: day 70-120
  What to look for: Active engagement — baby is now driving the interaction, not just responding.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/moves-to-get-attention/complete
